items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: I figured that there was another fellow by the name of Lewis Ogletree, who was right down there, this was at the Union. And I got him

ctx.x: I understand Lee Collins couldn't read too well.

Who that? No, he couldn't. I tried my best to teach Lee how to read, but he just barely spelled. And it's one thing that I'll never forget concerning Lee. See Lee and I were schoolmates too. And I had this, when I recorded in 1946, we still, still do. We'll get as many New Orleans musicians as possible. I mean until today. I just recorded a few days ago and we had Brother Montgomery, Oliver, Oliver Alcorn, myself, at least there was three of us at New Orleans. You still do it today, you know. And so Lee used to…
I understand they tried to put him in the rest of the spare for a while. Yeah.
